topic: Identifying what is still making calls with an application key
product_area: Account management / API and application keys
environment: Datadog organization with an application key created by a former employee
Application key shows recent last-used activity in the Application Keys UI
symptom_pattern: Customer sees an application key belonging to a former employee still showing recent usage and wants to know what is calling with it (IPs, API keys, etc.).
root_cause: All requests made with the application key during the past week came from a third-party secret-scanning service's infrastructure. The service ran a roughly daily cycle of calls using the application key together with one of the customer's API keys. Both source IPs were on the vendor's published egress address list.
resolution_path: Support engineer pulled internal Datadog HQ logs for requests made with the application key over the past week
Found the same five-call cycle repeating about once a day, with the same user agents and endpoints each time
Verified the two source IPs against the scanning vendor's published list of egress addresses
Identified which application key and which API key were being used together
Reported the findings to the customer, who then took the information to the right internal resources to track down the source on their side

tse_approach.summary: The support engineer pulled the key's usage from internal logs, grouped the requests into a repeating call pattern, and attributed them to a third-party scanner by checking the source IPs against the vendor's published list. They then gave the customer the pattern, the attribution and the paired API key.
steps: Reviewed internal HQ logs for the application key over the past week
Summarized the repeating five-call sequence with user agents, endpoints and status codes
Checked the source IPs against the vendor's published egress address list
Identified the application key and the API key used together
Sent a clear summary table to the customer and offered further help
Followed up after the customer confirmed the information was useful
communication: Opened with a short introduction, then gave a structured table of the request pattern and the key pairing. Explained how the source was verified (the vendor's published IP list) and closed by offering more help.
